title: How water safe is your family?
intro: Ten quick questions about how drowning really happens and what stops it. Most of them are things our family had to learn after the fact. Every answer comes with its source, and finishing prints a certificate.

questions.question: What is the leading cause of death for children ages 1 to 4 in the U.S.?
questions.explain: Drowning is the #1 cause of death for children ages 1 to 4. It’s also preventable.

questions.question: What does drowning usually look and sound like?
choices: Quiet, often with no splashing at all
questions.answer: Quiet, often with no splashing at all
questions.explain: Drowning happens in seconds and is often silent. There’s usually no splashing or calling for help, so you have to be watching to see it.

questions.question: How much water can a young child drown in?
questions.explain: Young children can drown in just an inch or two of water. Empty buckets, coolers and kiddie pools right after use, and stay within arm’s reach at bath time.

questions.question: Where do most young children drown in pools?
choices: At a home: their own, a grandparent’s, a friend’s or a neighbor’s
questions.answer: At a home: their own, a grandparent’s, a friend’s or a neighbor’s
questions.explain: More than 7 in 10 children who died in a pool or spa (2021–2023) drowned at a home. Grandparents’, neighbors’ and friends’ pools count too.

questions.question: How close should an adult be to a toddler who is in or near water?
questions.explain: Toddlers and weak swimmers need “touch supervision”: an adult within arm’s reach whenever they’re in or near water. Name one Water Watcher so everyone knows who’s on duty.

questions.question: Which pool fence protects children best?
choices: A fence on three sides, with the house as the fourth
A fence on all four sides that separates the pool from the house
No fence, if the pool has a floating cover
questions.answer: A fence on all four sides that separates the pool from the house
questions.explain: A fence that isolates the pool on all four sides lowers the odds of drowning by 83% compared with three-sided fencing. When the house is one side, a toddler can walk straight out the back door to the water.

questions.question: Are water wings and other “floaties” safety devices?
choices: No. Use a U.S. Coast Guard-approved life jacket instead
questions.answer: No. Use a U.S. Coast Guard-approved life jacket instead
questions.explain: Water wings and other floaties don’t prevent drowning and can slip off. A Coast Guard-approved life jacket protects better, and it still never replaces an adult watching.

questions.question: A young child is missing. Where should you look first?
choices: The water: the pool, spa, bathtub or pond
questions.answer: The water: the pool, spa, bathtub or pond
questions.explain: Check the water first, because seconds matter. In a CPSC study of young children who drowned in pools, 77% had been missing for 5 minutes or less.

questions.question: For every child who dies from drowning, how many more survive a drowning and need emergency care?
questions.explain: For every child lost to drowning, 7 more survive one and need emergency care. Some, like Adam, come home with injuries that change everything.

questions.question: After a drowning, what kind of CPR matters?
choices: No CPR: wait for the ambulance
questions.explain: After a drowning, fast CPR with rescue breaths matters. Call 911, and take an infant and child CPR class so you’re ready.

certificateText: took the Because of ADAM water safety quiz and knows that drowning is fast and silent, that toddlers need an adult within arm’s reach, that pools need a fence on all four sides, and that when a child is missing, you check the water first.
